newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher, but fail to pass 10,000.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher, but fail to pass 10,000.

text.p: Taiwan share prices failed to muster enough momentum to push past the 10,000-point barrier on Wednesday, but bargain-hunting on low priced shares still sent the index to a seven-year high close, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index pierced the 10,000 level in early trade, but dissipated late and ended at 9,942.79 for a gain of 50.45 points or 0.51 percent.
The close was the market's highest since it finished at 9,978.86 on April 12, 1990.
Turnover was strong at T$184.25 billion, but below the torrid T$200 billion-plus volumes in recent days.

Brokers said investors hunted for bargains on lower-priced export-oriented shares amid expectation that their products would become more competitive in international markets due to the recent weakening of the Taiwan dollar.
"The Taiwan dollar's fall should help boost exports," said Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities.
The Taiwan dollar on Tuesday fell below T$28 against one U.S. dollar for the first time since 1989, closing at T$28.17 reflecting a strong greenback overseas.
The local unit fell again at mid-session on Wednesday to T$28.339.
Textiles led the gains, rising four percent. Paper shares advanced 3.23 percent and Plastics closed 2.51 percent higher.
Recent rally-leading electronics, which lost 2.73 percent on Tuesday on heavy profit-taking, rebounded slightly with a 0.75 percent gain on Wednesday.
Financials lost 1.89 percent after the finance ministry on Wednesday began executing its plan to sell some 50 million shares of the "big three" state-run commercial banks in a privatisation scheme.
Brokers said the market's overall index would overcome the 10,000-point resistance in the near future.
"After all, the economic outlook in Taiwan is good," United Securities' Lin said. "This would help send the index above 10,000 points," United Securities' Lin said.
The government forecasts a gross domestic product growth of 6.24 percent for 1997.
A 9,900-10,500 trading range was seen for Thursday.
